title: Pass or Fail: Running a Scenario and Judging Every Step of the Trace Against Written Criteria

questions.question: Why must a scenario run end in a verdict and not in a plot?
options: A run passed by looking at it has no test behind it: next month's slow worsening is not looked at, and the verdict names the step and the criterion that failed
questions.explanation: The test fails on a non empty verdict and prints the list.

questions.question: Why is overshoot a fraction of the step's size?
options: So a big step and a small one can be compared, and the settling band, also a fraction of the step, means the same for both
questions.explanation: 2 percent of 1.5 is 0.03 and of 0.1 is 0.002.

questions.question: An underdamped step up and its exact mirror down are measured. What should the numbers be?
options: Identical, the same overshoot 0.0759, rise 0.1800 and settling 0.5600: past the target means the side the step was going toward
questions.explanation: A measurement that took past to mean above would report no overshoot going down.

questions.question: The target is changed to where the position already is. What should the analysis do?
options: Leave it out: it moves nothing, so there is no overshoot, rise or settling to report
questions.explanation: Four changes with one of no size and one beyond the end gave 2 steps.

questions.question: A loop oscillates for ever around its target. What does its settling time read, and what does the verdict say?
options: -1, which is not a time, and the verdict says settling: it never stayed within the band
questions.explanation: A pass for a loop that never settled would be a lie.

questions.question: The same scenario is run against a good sensor, one 60 ms late and one stuck from 1 s. What came out?
options: A pass, then failures on every step (overshoot, settling and final error), then failures on all but the overshoot of the last step, which did not move at all
Three failures of the same kind
questions.explanation: Each verdict said what it was about.
